title: Transform Trained Transformer for Accelerating Native 4K Video Generation
claim: Multi-scale attention windows over each axis share parameters, so each token reaches its full spatiotemporal context at low cost.
layout: 1 large panel, grid of circles, curved arrows from top-left token, labeled axes
description: A single large schematic shows a grid of circular tokens laid out along labeled H-axis (down), W-axis (right) and T-axis (diagonal) red arrows. Three nested rounded regions in orange, blue and green mark different attention scales. A query token F_{1,1} at top-left sends curved arrows to tokens at increasing offsets. Orange arrows reach the dense local window, blue arrows reach sparser mid-range tokens, and green arrows reach far-away tokens at the grid edges. Token labels such as F_{1+Δh2,1+Δw2} use subscript offset notation. A small legend at right shows orange, blue and green arrows sharing one origin, labeled 'Shared Parameters'. Green dots suggest further tokens beyond the grid. The eye goes first to the orange cluster and the fan of arrows from the top-left token. The crop does not include the caption's 4K sample images or the bar chart.
caption: 4K (2176$\times$3840) inference visualization: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B [ref] (81f), HunyuanVideo [ref] (41f), UltraGen [ref] (29f), and our T3-Video-T2V-1.3B (81f). Efficiency tests are performed on 81 frames with FlashAttention2 [ref] on a single H20 GPU. Bar chart: blue denotes theoretical $\mathrm{MACs}$ while orange denotes measured $latency$ of DiT in Wan2.1-1.3B [ref]. Vertical axis is on a logarithmic scale.
abstract: Native 4K (2176$\times$3840) video generation remains a critical challenge due to the quadratic computational explosion of full-attention as spatiotemporal resolution increases, making it difficult for models to strike a balance between efficiency and quality. This paper proposes a novel Transformer retrofit strategy termed T3 ($\textbf{T}$ransform $\textbf{T}$rained $\textbf{T}$ransformer) that, without altering the core architecture of full-attention pretrained models, significantly reduces compute requirements by optimizing their forward logic. Specifically, $\textbf{T3-Video}$ introduces a multi-scale weight-sharing window attention mechanism and, via hierarchical blocking together with an axis-preserving full-attention design, can effect an "attention pattern" transformation of a pretrained model using only modest compute and data. Results on $\textbf{4K-VBench}$ show that $\textbf{T3-Video}$ substantially outperforms existing approaches: while delivering performance improvements (+4.29$\uparrow$ VQA and +0.08$\uparrow$ VTC), it accelerates native 4K video generation by more than 10$\times$. Project page at https://zhangzjn.github.io/projects/T3-Video
